archetype.name: Pocket Passer (intermediate attacker)
archetype.definition: A tall, rhythm-based passer who wins from the pocket by driving the ball 10 to 20 yards downfield, especially off under-center action, and who has largely stopped using his legs as a weapon.

report.headline: Lawrence's accuracy jump is real; red-zone and third-down turnovers are the cost.
report.take:
This is the most efficient version of Trevor Lawrence we have seen. He is 6th in EPA per dropback at 0.214, 5th in yards per attempt at 8.45 and 8th in CPOE at 4.89. His career says that last number is new. He finished at -1.9 CPOE last year and -0.97 the year before, and even his 2022 peak sat at 1.4. Accuracy has never been his calling card, so a near-seven-point swing in CPOE from last season needs a cause. The charting supplies one. His bad-throw rate has fallen from 13.9% to 7.5%, 2nd-best among 45 charted passers, while his time to throw (2.88) is basically unchanged. He isn't getting the ball out faster or dinking more. He is simply putting it where it belongs.

The engine is the middle of the field and beyond. Throws of 10+ air yards produced 74 EPA, more than his entire dropback total of 69.2. The short game and screens behind the line are close to neutral, which is normal; what isn't normal is 0.457 EPA per attempt on intermediate throws and 0.784 deep. Liam Coen's offense also gets far more from him under center (0.424 EPA, 10.9 CPOE) than in shotgun (0.136, 1.0). Play-action and boot looks clearly suit him. Parker Washington (81 targets, 0.346 EPA per target) and Brenton Strange (0.361) are the main beneficiaries.

What the headline numbers smooth over is where the drives stall. His interception total ranks 43rd of 55, though the rate (2.3%) is mid-pack. Four of the seven came on third down and four on intermediate throws, the same window that makes him good. In the red zone he has 13 touchdowns but completes 44.8% with a -6.4 CPOE, so the scoring is coming from volume and field position more than precision. His rushing has also faded to 11.3 yards a game, almost ten fewer than last year. Designed runs are rare and he scrambles on just 3.3% of dropbacks.

The last three games are a mild cooling, not a collapse. EPA per dropback is down 0.059 from his season mark and CPOE is down 3.1, but most of that is one bad afternoon. At the Giants he went 25/47 with two picks, -6.6 EPA and a 3.56-second time to throw, his slowest of the year. Center Robert Hainsey (91% of snaps) is now out. The question for December is whether the clean pockets that let him go through progressions (pressured on 16.3% of dropbacks, 7th-lowest) survive a patched-up interior.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy
strengths.body: Throws of 10+ air yards produce 0.552 EPA per attempt with an 8.1 CPOE. Deep balls carry an 11.3 CPOE on 39 attempts. The deep number will cool on that sample, but it is backed by a bad-throw rate cut nearly in half from last year. That kind of change in ball placement tends to hold better than completion luck.

strengths.title: Under-center and play-action efficiency
strengths.body: From under center he is a different quarterback: 0.424 EPA per play, 71.4% completions and no interceptions on 70 attempts. Shotgun yields 0.136 EPA and all seven picks. This is a scheme fit Coen can keep leaning on, and it explains why the offense ranks 7th in pass EPA despite a slightly run-leaning pass rate.

strengths.title: Clean pockets, few sacks
strengths.body: He has been pressured on only 16.3% of dropbacks and is sacked on 5.3%, well under the 7.8% league average. That gives him time to work the middle of the field, where he posts 0.49 EPA per attempt. It depends on the line staying intact, which is now in question.

concerns.title: Third-down and intermediate interceptions
concerns.body: Four of his seven picks came on third down, where he faces an average of 8.8 yards to go and converts just 38.8%. Four also came on 10-19 yard throws. This is largely the price of his aggressiveness rather than a new flaw: he has finished bottom-tier in interceptions in four of five seasons. The rate is manageable; the timing (drive-killing downs) is the problem.

concerns.title: Red-zone precision lags
concerns.body: Inside the 20 he completes 44.8% with a -6.4 CPOE and 0.093 EPA per play, far below his overall efficiency. Thirteen touchdowns paper over it, but that count leans on volume and a strong offense around him. If the touchdowns slow, it will show here first.

concerns.title: Recent dip meets line injuries
concerns.body: His last three games run 0.059 EPA per dropback below his season, dragged down by a 47-attempt, two-interception loss at the Giants with a 3.56-second time to throw. Starting center Hainsey is out and left-side tackle Walker Little is questionable. That threatens the low-pressure environment his intermediate game relies on.

trend.note: He has posted positive passing EPA in eight of ten games, with peaks of 15.5 in Week 1 and 15.3 in Week 10. The only real duds were Denver and the Giants. Volume has climbed lately (36 attempts a game over the last three) while efficiency has slipped modestly.

nextGame.headline: Rematch with a pass defense he shredded two weeks ago
nextGame.body:
Tennessee is about as soft a pass defense as exists. It ranks 31st in pass EPA allowed (0.229), dead last in explosive pass rate and 30th on short throws. It also allows 303.2 passing yards a game to quarterbacks, 32nd. In Week 10 he threw for 352 yards, three touchdowns and 15.3 EPA in Nashville with a 2.9% bad-throw rate. The one structural risk is game script. Jacksonville is a 14.5-point home favorite with the league's 2nd-ranked defense, and offenses tend to run more than usual against Tennessee. A Week 8-style blowout, when he threw just 14 passes, would cap his volume even if every throw is efficient.

Availability cuts both ways. On his side, losing Hainsey matters most because it weakens the interior protection behind his middle-of-the-field game. Little and running back Bhayshul Tuten are questionable; Tuten's absence would tilt more early-down work toward the pass. Tennessee's pass rush is weak, though (26th in hit rate, 21st in sack rate), which softens the line concern. Cornerback Cor'Dale Flott (89% of snaps) is questionable with a neck injury. If he sits, an already porous secondary gets thinner on the outside.

keyMatchups.title: Washington against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Tennessee lets lead receivers score 6.4 PPR points a game above their norms, 31st in the league, and allows 0.55 EPA per WR1 target. Parker Washington is his most-targeted and most productive receiver. Expect the offense to feed that matchup early.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive plays against Tennessee's secondary
keyMatchups.body: His best throws are 10+ air yards, and Tennessee allows the highest explosive pass rate in the league. Last meeting he threw for 352 yards. The deep shots should be there in the first half.

keyMatchups.title: Blowout script caps volume
keyMatchups.body: At -14.5 with an elite defense behind him, a lopsided score could pull the offense into the run game by the third quarter. In the Week 8 blowout of Indianapolis he attempted only 14 passes and played 81% of snaps.

nextGame.watch: How quickly he gets the ball out with a backup center. If his time to throw creeps back toward the Giants-game 3.56, the efficiency edge erodes even against a bad defense.

restOfSeason.body:
The core of this season should hold. A bad-throw rate cut nearly in half and a scheme that keeps him under center and attacking the intermediate middle are durable foundations. He should stay a top-10 passer by efficiency. What will regress is the extreme stuff: an 11.3 deep CPOE on 39 attempts and a 7.2% touchdown rate that his red-zone accuracy doesn't fully support. Expect efficiency closer to 0.12-0.20 EPA per dropback and touchdowns nearer 1.5-2.2 a game than his current pace.

Volume is capped by context. Jacksonville runs slightly more than expected, and its defense will put it ahead often. That means plenty of games like Week 8, where he isn't needed late. The interception rate looks like who he has always been, so pencil in steady picks. The rushing floor of earlier seasons is mostly gone, which lowers his fantasy ceiling unless the team lets him run again. The offensive line's health over the next few weeks is the biggest variable.
swingFactors: Hainsey's return and the interior line's health
Whether red-zone accuracy catches up to the touchdown count

confidence.note: Ten games with a clear charting cause for the accuracy jump, but deep and red-zone splits rest on small samples and the line is banged up.
